root_causes.description: Frontend trace data shows abnormally long request durations (~15s spans, p95 ~30s) on user_browse_product and user_get_recommendations flows, which can force client timeouts and surface as frontend errors. This is a plausible alternative if the injected fault is latency rather than an explicit abort.

root_causes.description: The slow recommendation/browse flows in frontend traces traverse the recommendation → product-catalog path, so a fault in this downstream chain could drive frontend timeouts. However, both recommendation and product-catalog report zero server errors, making this a weaker hypothesis.

remediation_steps: Inspect frontend pod logs and access logs during 04:40–08:10 UTC for aborted/5xx responses to confirm local request abortion.
Identify any chaos/fault injection applied to the frontend workload (e.g., HTTP abort experiment) in the otel-demo namespace and roll it back.
Verify frontend readiness/health probes and rolling-restart the frontend deployment to clear any stuck aborted-request state.
Add alerting on frontend error-rate and 15s+ browse/recommendation request durations to catch recurrence early.
If latency-driven, review frontend timeouts and the recommendation → product-catalog call path for upstream timeout misconfiguration.
